transcript:
T01 [00:00] Agent: Hello, may I speak to Priya Malhotra, please? I'm calling from vehicle finance collections.
T02 [00:05] Customer: Speaking.
T03 [00:07] Agent: Before we go any further, please confirm your full name, date of birth and the first line of your address with the postcode.
T04 [00:15] Customer: Priya Malhotra, second of March nineteen ninety-one. 41 Linden Drive, Derby, DE22 4QT.
T05 [00:24] Agent: Thank you, that all matches, so security is complete. I'm calling about the instalment due on the first of November, which hasn't been received.
T06 [00:35] Customer: I know. My hours at the warehouse dropped. I'm on a zero-hour contract and they've only given me two shifts a week since October.
T07 [00:47] Agent: I'm sorry to hear that. Roughly how much has that changed your monthly income?
T08 [00:53] Customer: About three hundred pounds less than usual.
T09 [00:58] Agent: Thank you. Would you be able to make a payment towards the missed instalment today?
T10 [01:04] Customer: Not today, I've got nothing spare until I'm paid. I get paid on Friday.
T11 [01:11] Agent: Understood. What could you afford on Friday?
T12 [01:15] Customer: Ninety pounds. I can do that through the online portal.
T13 [01:22] Agent: So that's ninety pounds through the online portal on Friday the thirteenth of November. Is that affordable after your rent and food?
T14 [01:33] Customer: Yes, I've worked it out. The rent's covered.
T15 [01:39] Agent: Thank you. I should explain that while the account is in arrears it may be reported to credit reference agencies, which could affect your credit file.
T16 [01:51] Customer: Okay, I understand.
T17 [01:55] Agent: Just to check, can you tell me what you've agreed to today?
T18 [02:00] Customer: Ninety pounds on the portal on Friday, and you'll call me after that.
T19 [02:08] Agent: That's right. We'll call you on Tuesday the seventeenth of November after six to review the remaining arrears and your shifts.
T20 [02:19] Customer: After six is fine. I finish at half five.
T21 [02:25] Agent: If your hours change before then, please contact us. Is there anything else I can help with?
T22 [02:33] Customer: No, that's everything. Thanks.
summary: DPA completed. The company called and reached the customer, and arrears were discussed. The customer's zero-hour contract has provided only two shifts a week since October, reducing monthly income by £300; the agent attempted to secure a payment, but the customer declined until payday. Possible credit file impact was explained, the agent checked the customer's understanding, and the customer agreed to pay £90 through the online portal on 13 November. The next steps are for the company to call on 17 November after 6 pm to review the remaining arrears and the customer's shifts.

transcript:
T01 [00:00] Agent: Good afternoon, vehicle finance customer services, how can I help?
T02 [00:04] Customer: Hi, I'm ringing about my car finance. I missed this month's payment and I want to sort it out.
T03 [00:11] Agent: I can help with that. Can you confirm your full name, date of birth and address including the postcode?
T04 [00:18] Customer: Daniel Okafor, twenty-first of June nineteen eighty-four. 7 Brook Lane, Swindon, SN2 6PL.
T05 [00:27] Agent: Thank you, Mr Okafor, you're verified. I can see one missed instalment and arrears on the account. What happened?
T06 [00:36] Customer: My bank froze my account after a fraud alert. The direct debit bounced while they were investigating.
T07 [00:45] Agent: That sounds stressful. Has the bank resolved it?
T08 [00:49] Customer: They unfroze it yesterday. Everything's back to normal and my wages went in fine.
T09 [00:56] Agent: Good. Would you like to pay the missed instalment today by debit card?
T10 [01:02] Customer: Yes please, let's clear it now.
T11 [01:06] Agent: I'll transfer you to our secure payment line. Thank you for waiting, that payment has gone through successfully.
T12 [01:41] Customer: Great. Will the normal direct debit still come out?
T13 [01:46] Agent: Yes, your direct debit stays the same. The next collection is on the fourth of December.
T14 [01:54] Customer: The fourth. Okay, the money will be there.
T15 [01:59] Agent: I'll email you a payment confirmation today. Can I just check you're clear on what happens next?
T16 [02:07] Customer: Yes. The missed one's paid now, and the normal payment comes out on the fourth of December.
T17 [02:16] Agent: Exactly. If anything changes with your bank before then, give us a call.
T18 [02:23] Customer: Will do. Thanks for your help.
summary: DPA completed. The customer called the company and arrears were discussed. The bank froze the customer's account after a fraud alert, causing the Direct Debit to be returned; the account has since been unfrozen. Payment made, the agent checked the customer's understanding, and the existing Direct Debit continues with the next collection on 14 December. The next steps are to check the emailed payment confirmation and contact the company if anything changes with the bank before then.

transcript:
T01 [00:00] Agent: Good morning, vehicle finance collections. How can I help?
T02 [00:04] Customer: Morning. I'm calling about my account. My wife's here with me on speaker, she handles our bills.
T03 [00:11] Agent: That's fine. First, can I take your full name, date of birth and postcode?
T04 [00:16] Customer: Gareth Hughes, ninth of September nineteen seventy-nine, CF14 3RJ.
T05 [00:24] Agent: And the first line of your address?
T06 [00:27] Customer: 52 Elm Terrace.
T07 [00:30] Agent: Thank you, Mr Hughes, that's all verified. Are you happy for me to discuss the account with your wife today?
T08 [00:37] Customer: Yes, she can talk about everything on the account.
T09 [00:41] Agent: Thank you. Can I take her name, please? I'll record your authority for her to act on this call.
T10 [00:48] Third party: It's Carys Hughes.
T11 [00:51] Agent: Thank you, Mrs Hughes, authority to act is recorded for this call. There are two missed instalments on the account.
T12 [01:00] Third party: Yes, that's why we rang. We had a boiler breakdown at home and the repair was six hundred and fifty pounds, so we fell behind.
T13 [01:12] Agent: I'm sorry to hear that. Have your incomes changed at all?
T14 [01:17] Customer: No, both our jobs are the same. It was just the boiler.
T15 [01:23] Agent: Would you like to arrange a payment towards the arrears?
T16 [01:28] Third party: We can pay one hundred and sixty pounds on the twentieth of November when Gareth gets paid, by bank transfer.
T17 [01:38] Agent: Thank you. So that's one hundred and sixty pounds by bank transfer on the twentieth of November, using your account reference. Is that affordable?
T18 [01:50] Customer: Yes, we've budgeted for it.
T19 [01:54] Agent: I need to let you know that if the arrears aren't cleared, the account is at risk of further action, which could include a default notice.
T20 [02:06] Customer: Understood. We'll get it sorted.
T21 [02:10] Agent: We'll call on the twenty-third of November to confirm the transfer has arrived and agree how to clear the rest.
T22 [02:20] Third party: That's fine. Thanks.
summary: DPA completed. The customer called the company with their wife, whose Authority to Act was verified for this call, and arrears were discussed. A boiler repair costing £650 caused the missed instalments, and household income was otherwise unchanged. The customer was warned that the account is at risk of further action, including a default notice, and agreed to pay £180 by bank transfer on 20 November using their account reference. The next steps are for the company to call on 23 November to confirm receipt and agree how to clear the remaining arrears.

transcript:
T01 [00:00] Agent: Hello, could I speak to Martin Doyle, please? I'm calling from vehicle finance collections.
T02 [00:05] Customer: Yes, that's me.
T03 [00:07] Agent: Before we discuss the account, please confirm your full name, date of birth and the first line of your address with the postcode.
T04 [00:15] Customer: Martin Doyle, fifteenth of January nineteen sixty-eight. 3 Harbour View, Plymouth, PL4 0DX.
T05 [00:24] Agent: Thank you, those details match and security is complete. I'm calling because the last instalment wasn't received and the account is in arrears.
T06 [00:34] Customer: I'm sorry. My wife passed away three weeks ago. Our joint account was frozen by the bank and I can't get at the money until probate is sorted.
T07 [00:48] Agent: I'm very sorry for your loss. Thank you for telling me. Would it be all right for me to make a note of your bereavement and the frozen account, so we can support you properly?
T08 [01:01] Customer: Yes, please do. I don't want to have to explain it again.
T09 [01:07] Agent: Thank you, I've noted that with your consent. Is there any money coming in at the moment?
T10 [01:14] Customer: Just my pension. It covers food and the council tax, but there's nothing left after that.
T11 [01:24] Agent: I understand, and I won't ask for a payment today. Have you heard of StepChange? They give free, independent debt advice and can help while things are sorted.
T12 [01:37] Customer: I haven't. I'd appreciate that.
T13 [01:41] Agent: There's also a bereavement support page on our website with their contact details and other help.
T14 [01:49] Customer: Thank you. My daughter can look at that with me.
T15 [01:54] Agent: I'm going to put a thirty-day hold on collection contact so you have time to get advice and deal with the bank.
T16 [02:04] Customer: That would really help.
T17 [02:08] Agent: The hold pauses our calls and letters, but the arrears will still be on the account. Does that make sense?
T18 [02:17] Customer: Yes. The money's still owed, you just won't chase me for a month.
T19 [02:24] Agent: That's right. We'll call you on the eleventh of December, after the hold, to see how things are.
T20 [02:33] Customer: Thank you for being so understanding.
summary: DPA completed. The company called and reached the customer, and arrears were discussed. The customer's wife died three weeks ago and the bank froze their joint account until probate is resolved, leaving only a pension that covers food and council tax with nothing left over; Consent gained to record vulnerability. The customer was referred to StepChange and customer signposted to the company website, and the agent checked understanding that the hold does not clear the arrears. A thirty-day hold on collection contact was applied, and the next steps are to seek advice and deal with the bank before the company calls on 11 December.
